cards.title: Alliteration
cards.notes: Repetition of the same initial consonant sound in nearby words.

fields.Definition: Repetition of the same initial consonant sound in nearby words.
fields.Example: "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers."

cards.title: Anaphora
cards.notes: Repetition of a word or phrase at the beginning of successive clauses.

fields.Definition: Repetition of a word or phrase at the beginning of successive clauses.
fields.Example: "I have a dream... I have a dream..." — Martin Luther King Jr.

cards.title: Epistrophe
cards.notes: Repetition of a word or phrase at the end of successive clauses.

fields.Definition: Repetition of a word or phrase at the end of successive clauses.
fields.Example: "...of the people, by the people, for the people." — Lincoln

cards.title: Antithesis
cards.notes: Juxtaposition of contrasting ideas in parallel grammatical structure.

fields.Definition: Juxtaposition of contrasting ideas in parallel grammatical structure.
fields.Example: "It was the best of times, it was the worst of times." — Dickens

cards.title: Chiasmus
cards.notes: Reversal of grammatical structures in successive phrases.

fields.Definition: Reversal of grammatical structures in successive phrases.
fields.Example: "Ask not what your country can do for you — ask what you can do for your country."

cards.title: Metaphor
cards.notes: Direct comparison between unlike things, stating one is the other.

fields.Definition: Direct comparison between unlike things, stating one is the other.
fields.Example: "Life is a highway."

cards.title: Simile
cards.notes: Comparison using 'like' or 'as'.

fields.Definition: Comparison using 'like' or 'as'.
fields.Example: "He fought like a lion."

cards.title: Personification
cards.notes: Giving human qualities, actions, or emotions to non-human things.

fields.Definition: Giving human qualities, actions, or emotions to non-human things.
fields.Example: "The wind whispered through the trees."

cards.title: Hyperbole
cards.notes: Deliberate, extreme exaggeration not meant to be taken literally.

fields.Definition: Deliberate, extreme exaggeration not meant to be taken literally.
fields.Example: "I've told you a million times!"

cards.title: Litotes
cards.notes: Understatement through double negation or negating the contrary.

fields.Definition: Understatement through double negation or negating the contrary.
fields.Example: "Not bad" (meaning very good). "Einstein was no dummy."

cards.title: Irony
cards.notes: Saying the opposite of what is meant, often for humorous or emphatic effect.

fields.Definition: Saying the opposite of what is meant, often for humorous or emphatic effect.
fields.Example: "What a beautiful day!" [said in a hurricane]

cards.title: Rhetorical Question
cards.notes: A question asked for effect with no answer expected.

fields.Definition: A question asked for effect with no answer expected.
fields.Example: "Et tu, Brute?" — Shakespeare

cards.title: Synecdoche
cards.notes: Using a part to represent the whole, or the whole to represent a part.

fields.Definition: Using a part to represent the whole, or the whole to represent a part.
fields.Example: "All hands on deck" (hands = sailors)

cards.title: Metonymy
cards.notes: Using an associated concept or word to refer to something else.

fields.Definition: Using an associated concept or word to refer to something else.
fields.Example: "The Crown announced a new policy" (Crown = monarchy)

cards.title: Allusion
cards.notes: An indirect reference to a well-known person, place, event, or text.

fields.Definition: An indirect reference to a well-known person, place, event, or text.
fields.Example: "He had a Midas touch with every business venture."

cards.title: Parallelism
cards.notes: Use of structurally similar grammatical elements in a series.

fields.Definition: Use of structurally similar grammatical elements in a series.
fields.Example: "He came, he saw, he conquered."

cards.title: Oxymoron
cards.notes: Two contradictory terms placed directly together.

fields.Definition: Two contradictory terms placed directly together.
fields.Example: "Bittersweet." "Deafening silence." "Living death."

cards.title: Paradox
cards.notes: A statement that seems contradictory but upon reflection reveals a truth.

fields.Definition: A statement that seems contradictory but upon reflection reveals a truth.
fields.Example: "The more you know, the more you realize you know nothing."

cards.title: Asyndeton
cards.notes: Deliberate omission of conjunctions between clauses for speed or impact.

fields.Definition: Deliberate omission of conjunctions between clauses for speed or impact.
fields.Example: "I came, I saw, I conquered."

cards.title: Polysyndeton
cards.notes: Deliberate use of many conjunctions in quick succession.

fields.Definition: Deliberate use of many conjunctions in quick succession.
fields.Example: "We lived and laughed and loved and left."

cards.title: Euphemism
cards.notes: Substituting a mild or indirect expression for one thought to be harsh.

fields.Definition: Substituting a mild or indirect expression for one thought to be harsh.
fields.Example: "Passed away" for died. "Collateral damage" for civilian casualties.

cards.title: Onomatopoeia
cards.notes: Words that phonetically imitate or resemble the sound they describe.

fields.Definition: Words that phonetically imitate or resemble the sound they describe.
fields.Example: "Buzz, hiss, crackle, murmur, sizzle."

cards.title: Apostrophe
cards.notes: Directly addressing an absent person, a dead person, or an abstraction.

fields.Definition: Directly addressing an absent person, a dead person, or an abstraction.
fields.Example: "O Death, where is thy sting?" — 1 Corinthians 15:55

cards.title: Zeugma
cards.notes: One word (usually a verb) governs or applies to two or more words differently.

fields.Definition: One word (usually a verb) governs or applies to two or more words differently.
fields.Example: "She broke his car and his heart."

cards.title: Aposiopesis
cards.notes: Breaking off mid-sentence, leaving a thought unfinished for effect.

fields.Definition: Breaking off mid-sentence, leaving a thought unfinished for effect.
fields.Example: "Why you little—!" [trails off in anger]
